title: Reports of Fraudulent or Counterfeit Merchandise Sold on E-commerce Platforms
what_it_is: Reports of Fraudulent or Counterfeit Merchandise Sold on E-commerce Platforms

sections.label: Police assessment of counterfeit goods
sections.summary: Police assess criminal offences from full facts; buyers may seek recourse via CASE, Small Claims Tribunal or civil proceedings, and Police do not track the requested data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Police assess whether any criminal offence is disclosed by looking at the full facts and circumstances of each case.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, the import, sale, or distribution of goods with falsely applied trademarks for the purpose of trade is an offence under the Trade Marks Act 1998.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Where deception is involved, the case may also be classified as "cheating" under section 420 of the Penal Code 1871.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Regardless of whether a criminal offence is disclosed, buyers can seek recourse by lodging a complaint with the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE), filing a claim in the Small Claims Tribunal, or commencing civil proceedings in the Singapore Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Police do not track the data requested by the Member.

sections.label: Seller knowledge in counterfeit cases
sections.summary: If a seller did not know goods were counterfeit, cheating may not apply; if the seller knew, the case may fall under the Trade Marks Act and section 420 cheating.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Coming back to the example that he had shared where there was a merchandise that was advertised as genuine but was subsequently found to be counterfeit, there could be an instance whereby the seller either knew in the first place whether the merchandise was genuine or not.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, through Police investigations, if it was found that the seller did not know that the merchandise was actually counterfeit, then, a cheating offence may not be the means in which to charge the individual.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If, however, the individual knew it was counterfeit – and this is found out through the course of Police investigations – but the seller still chooses to advertise the merchandise as a genuine product, then, this would be a case under both the Trade Marks Act as well as classified as cheating under section 420 of the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If the victim, his resident, find difficulties with the legal fees, she can approach Legal Aid to explore the options.
